name: Adam and Eve
charge: Eating from the tree God forbade
summary: Adam received the command not to eat of the forbidden tree. The serpent contradicted its warning of death, the woman took and ate and gave to her husband, and he ate also. They covered themselves and hid, then answered God's inquiry by shifting blame. Judgment brought sorrow, toil, mortality, and expulsion; God clothed them before driving them out.
offense: The command and the contradiction stand against each other. God told Adam that eating of the forbidden tree would bring death; the serpent told the woman that they would not surely die (Genesis 2:16-17; Genesis 3:4-5). The temptation offered wisdom while denying the consequence of disobedience. Its doctrine was that the commandment could be broken without the judgment God had spoken. The fruit of lies is the spiritual danger: a word received becomes a deed performed (Hosea 10:13). Eve saw what was desirable, took, ate, and gave to her husband, and he ate also (Genesis 3:6). Paul warns of minds corrupted as the serpent beguiled Eve, and of Satan appearing as an angel of light (2 Corinthians 11:3,14). The promise of enlightenment did not make the teaching true. Adam's charge was that he hearkened to his wife against the command given to him (Genesis 3:17); another person's persuasion did not remove his responsibility.
judgment: Their covering and hiding could not answer God's inquiry. Job speaks of covering transgressions as Adam, and Lamentations joins exposed nakedness to grievous sin (Job 31:33; Lamentations 1:8). The call, Where art thou, brought the man to account. Adam pointed to the woman God had given him, and she pointed to the serpent, but each still had to answer for the deed (Genesis 3:9-13). The serpent was cursed and brought low, and enmity was appointed between his seed and the woman's seed (Genesis 3:14-15). The promise reaches to Christ's destruction of the devil's works and the bruising of Satan under the saints' feet (1 John 3:8; Romans 16:20). To the woman came multiplied sorrow; to Adam, toil upon cursed ground until his return to dust (Genesis 3:16-19). The lie had promised escape from death, but the sentence established the opposite. God clothed them with coats of skins before driving them out (Genesis 3:21-24). The covering points toward the need for an atonement they could not supply by hiding; the Lamb is the provision named in Revelation 13:8. Mercy in their clothing did not cancel their expulsion. The guarded way to the tree of life left them unable to take for themselves what disobedience had forfeited.

verses.text: And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;
In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
And the Lord God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.
So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.
For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.
Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law (also) in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still.

entries.commentary: This is the first Sabbath that you read about in the scriptures. The Most High blessed the seventh day and sanctified it.
Chapter 2 is the manner of creation. It goes back through what you read in chapter 1 and gives you more detail on certain things.

Here is the detail on how man was formed: the Most High formed him of the dust of the ground. The breath of life is talking about the commandments. This is Adam, the chosen. Out of all the people the Most High created on the earth, He had a favorite from the beginning.
The Most High planted the garden eastward in Eden and put the chosen man there. The river Gihon is the Blue Nile; it compasses the whole land of Ethiopia.
Some of these trees are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men.
The Most High looked at the women on the earth and there was no help meet right for Adam. This again shows there were more people on the earth than Adam alone.
The Most High created Eve from Adam because there was no woman on the earth right for him at that time.

Chapter 3 deals with the craftiness of your enemy. This is not a literal snake. Another word for serpent is deceiver; the serpent is Satan. You know it is not a literal serpent because serpents do not speak.

Satan taught Eve doctrine. She had been taught that if she broke the commandments of the Most High she would die; the serpent now taught her that she would not die. The same doctrine is taught today: that your eyes will be opened and you do not have to keep the commandments and you will not die. If you leave the commandments you are going to die.

Any time scripture speaks of good for food like this, it is talking about good to learn. The fruit she ate was the lies. She was enticed to break the commandments of the Most High, then she went and taught her husband the same thing the serpent taught her, and he broke the commandments as well.
They were not literally naked; nakedness represents sin. They were in sin. Remember this is an illustrated story. The fig leaves and aprons represent them trying to cover their transgressions.
The trees of the garden here are people. Adam and his wife tried to hide their sins among the other people that were in the garden with them.

The Most High was not looking for Adam as though He could not find him; He was calling Adam to examine himself. Adam had started to separate himself from the Most High by covering and hiding his sins, and the Most High already knew what he had done.
Adam blamed Eve for his sin, and in saying the woman whom thou gavest he blamed the Most High also. Then Eve blamed the serpent; they played the blame game.

The cattle and the beasts of the field here are the nations. Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

This is a prophecy. It is not talking about the serpent and Eve; the woman is the nation of Israel. The woman does not plant seed; the man plants seed. The Most High is saying He will put enmity between Satan's seed and Israel's seed, and that enmity remains. Christ was to come from the woman. [Revelation 12](/bible/revelation/12) explains this verse. Bruising the heel is making Israel stumble. When a serpent strikes at your heel you stumble; Satan makes Israel stumble through evil communication and corrupting good manners. It shall bruise thy head is spoken to the serpent: Christ was going to come and destroy the works of Satan.

Your desire, your learning, your desire of anything was to be to your husband, and he shall rule over thee. This is one of the first commandments given, alongside be fruitful and multiply, the Sabbath, and the commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Sisters, if you do not allow your husband to rule over you, it does not matter what else you keep; you are not entering the kingdom without fulfilling this.
Because Adam hearkened to his wife and broke the commandment, the ground was cursed for his sake; in sorrow and sweat he would eat of it all his days.

This is animal sacrifice to cover the sins. This is where the Most High ordained the sacrificial law; this is when they started to sacrifice. The first sacrifice is twofold. A literal lamb was slain here to clothe Adam and his wife, and that lamb slain from the foundation of the world represents Christ, slain for our sins.
The man was driven out of the garden to till the ground from whence he was taken, and the way of the tree of life was kept.

In the thirtieth year after the ruin of the city I was in Babylon, and lay troubled upon my bed, and my thoughts came up over my heart. I saw the desolation of Sion, and the wealth of them that dwelt at Babylon; and my spirit was sore moved, so that I began to speak words full of fear to the most High. Thou gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. Unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way, which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations. In process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them; nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.

When they that dwelt upon the earth began to multiply, they began again to be more ungodly than the first. Thou didst choose thee a man from among them, whose name was Abraham: him thou lovedst, and made an everlasting covenant with him, promising him that thou wouldest never forsake his seed. Unto him thou gavest Isaac, and unto Isaac thou gavest Jacob and Esau: as for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau. When thou leddest his seed out of Egypt, thou broughtest them up to the mount Sinai, and bowing the heavens thou didst set fast the earth, and madest the depths to tremble. Thy glory went through four gates, of fire, and of earthquake, and of wind, and of cold; that thou mightest give the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel.

Yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart, that thy law might bring forth fruit in them. For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law also in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still. Thou raisedst up a servant, called David, whom thou commandedst to build a city unto thy name, and to offer incense and oblations unto thee therein. When this was done many years, then they that inhabited the city forsook thee, and in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done; and so thou gavest the city over into the hands of thine enemies.

Are their deeds any better that inhabit Babylon, that they should therefore have the dominion over Sion? When I came thither, and had seen impieties without number, then my soul saw many evildoers in this thirtieth year, so that my heart failed me. I have seen how thou sufferest them sinning, and hast spared the wicked doers, and hast destroyed thy people, and hast preserved thine enemies. Are they then of Babylon better than they of Sion? or is there any other people that knoweth thee beside Israel? or what generation hath so believed thy covenants as Jacob? For I have gone here and there through the heathen, and I see that they flow in wealth, and think not upon thy commandments. Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and theirs also that dwell in the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel. Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
